in_hebrew.name: אוסביוס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם אוסביוס נגזר מהמילה היוונית 'אוספוס', שפירושה 'אדיקות' או 'פחד אלוהים'. הוא משמש לתיאור אדם בעל אדיקות עמוקה ומחויבות לדת. השם משמש גם כהתייחסות לאדם בעל מוסר ואינטגריטציה גבוהים.

in_greek.name: Εὐσέβιος
in_greek.long_meaning: Τὸ ὄνομα Εὐσέβιος προέρχεται ἀπὸ τὴν ἑλληνικὴ λέξη 'εὐσέβεια', ἡ ὁποία σημαίνει 'ἀρετή' ἢ 'θρησκευτικότητα'. Σημαίνει ἄνθρωπο μὲ βαθειὰ εὐσέβεια καὶ δέσμευση πρὸς τὴν θρησκεία. Ἐπίσης, ὁ ὅρος χρησιμοποιεῖται γιὰ νὰ περιγράψει ἄνθρωπο μὲ ὑψηλὴ ἠθικὴ καὶ ἀκεραιότητα.

in_latin.name: Eusebios
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Eusebios derivatur a verbo Graeco 'εὐσέβεια', quod significat 'pietas' aut 'devotio'. Designat hominem qui habet profundam pietatem et devotionem ad Deum. Terminus etiam adhibetur ad describendum hominem qui habet alta moralia et integritatem.

in_english.name: Eusebios
in_english.long_meaning: The name Eusebios originates from the Greek word 'εὐσέβεια' (eusebeia), meaning 'piety' or 'devotion'. It signifies a person of deep religious devotion, moral integrity, and spiritual commitment. Historically, the name has been associated with early Christian tradition and is borne by several notable saints, including Eusebius of Vercelli and Eusebius of Caesarea, a prominent Church historian.

saint_reference.note: Eusebius of Vercelli was a 4th-century bishop and saint known for his piety and defense of orthodoxy.

data.cultural_impact: The name Eusebios holds strong historical and cultural significance in Greek and Christian traditions. Eusebios was the name of several early Christian saints and scholars, including Eusebius of Caesarea, the prominent early Church historian and theologian. His writings, such as "The History of the Church," greatly influenced Christian theology and are still studied today.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Eusebios is imbued with spiritual significance and speaks to the deep reverence and devotion to God that characterizes a God-loved and God-dedicated soul. Naming a child Eusebios conveys the parents' hope that their child will follow in the footsteps of the saints bearing this name, becoming a righteous, pious, and devout individual in their own community and in the sight of God. This name serves as a daily reminder of the importance of fostering a deep and enduring love and connection with the divine.

historical_references.reference: Eusebius of Caesarea was a prominent early Christian historian and theologian, known for his ecclesiastical history. He was born around 260 AD in Palestine and died around 339 AD. He played a significant role in the development of early Christian theology and the formation of the Orthodox Church. Eusebius authored several influential works, including his Ecclesiastical History and his commentary on the Psalms. His writings were important sources for later historians such as Sozomen and Socrates Scholasticus.

Eusebius of Vercelli was a bishop of Vercelli in northern Italy in the late 4th century AD. He was born around 303 AD and died around 371 AD. He was a prominent figure in the Arian Controversy, a theological dispute over the nature of Christ. Eusebius of Vercelli was an advocate of Arianism, which held that Jesus was a created being and not coeternal with God the Father. He was exiled several times by the Roman Emperor Valentinian I for his beliefs. Despite his controversial views, Eusebius of Vercelli is remembered for his role in the development of the Arian movement and his efforts to spread Christianity in northern Italy.
historical_references.context: Prominent figure in the Arian Controversy and advocate of Arianism

modern_usage.modern_context: Eusebios of Caesarea (260-339 AD), a prominent early Christian historian and scholar, is a subject of extensive research in the fields of Byzantine history, Early Christian scholars, and Ancient Greek studies. His works, including Church History, Onomasticon, and Preparation for the Gospel, have been widely studied and are available on various academic platforms such as Academia.edu, Google Scholar, and JSTOR.
